# Celestine ![Crystal CI](https://github.com/celestinecr/celestine/workflows/Crystal%20CI/badge.svg) [![Documentation badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-latest-green.svg?style=flat-square)](https://docs.celestine.dev)


[![Celestine Logo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/celestinecr/celestine/main/logo/logo.svg)](https://github.com/celestinecr/celestine/blob/main/src/make_logo.cr)


A neat library and DSL for creating graphics using SVG

## Installation

Add to shards.yml

```yaml
dependencies:
  celestine:
    github: celestinecr/celestine
```

## Docs

Documentation is cool, you can view the docs for Celestine at:
 * [**docs.celestine.dev**](https://docs.celestine.dev/)

## SVG Stuff It Can Do

A full list is [here](https://docs.celestine.dev/svg_element_checklist.html).

 * Finish adding all filters
 * Add pattern
 * Add gradients

## Examples

If you'd like to see how the logo was made, check out [make_logo](https://github.com/celestinecr/celestine/blob/main/src/make_logo.cr)

Here are some more intricate examples. [procedural_art](https://github.com/sol-vin/procedural_art)

Real world examples made with Celestine. All of these are flat SVG files with no JS inside, using only functions built into Celestine.

 * [Inward](https://www.sol.vin/art/live/inward/)
 * [Mineshift](https://www.sol.vin/art/live/mineshift/)
 * [Hypnos1](https://cdpn.io/redcodefinal/fullpage/ZEOgzXX)

## Community Examples

These are some examples of cool stuff other people have done with Celestine!

 * [sunrise](https://sunrise.sugarfi.dev) @ [github](https://github.com/sugarfi/sunrise) by [SugarFi](https://sugarfi.dev)
   * Uses the very strong Turbulence and DisplacementMap filters to create a very neat water effect.

## Development

HMU via issues or make a pull request or something I don't know.

## Contributing

1. Fork it (<https://github.com/celestinecr/celestine/fork>)
2. Create your feature branch (`git checkout -b my-new-feature`)
3. Commit your changes (`git commit -am 'Add some feature'`)
4. Push to the branch (`git push origin my-new-feature`)
5. Create a new Pull Request to the `development` branch at celestinecr/celestine

elsif to

end

end

if inner_elements.empty?
  io << "/>"
else
  io << ">"
  io << inner_elements
  io << "</#{TAG}>"
end

types.name: Color
types.doc: Represents an RGBA/HSLA color with parsing, conversions, and manipulation utilities.
types.summary: Represents an RGBA/HSLA color with parsing, conversions, and manipulation utilities.

def.name: hex
def.body:
s = str.lstrip('#')
case s.size
when 3
  r = (s[0].to_s * 2).to_u8(16)
  g = (s[1].to_s * 2).to_u8(16)
  b = (s[2].to_s * 2).to_u8(16)
  new(r, g, b, 1.0)
when 4
  r = (s[0].to_s * 2).to_u8(16)
  g = (s[1].to_s * 2).to_u8(16)
  b = (s[2].to_s * 2).to_u8(16)
  a = ((s[3].to_s * 2).to_u8(16)) / 255.0
  new(r, g, b, a)
when 6
  r = s[0..1].to_u8(16)
  g = s[2..3].to_u8(16)
  b = s[4..5].to_u8(16)
  new(r, g, b, 1.0)
when 8
  r = s[0..1].to_u8(16)
  g = s[2..3].to_u8(16)
  b = s[4..5].to_u8(16)
  a = (s[6..7].to_u8(16)) / 255.0
  new(r, g, b, a)
else
  raise(ArgumentError.new("Invalid hex color format: #{str}"))
end

def.name: to_hsl
def.body:
r1 = @r.to_f64 / 255.0
g1 = @g.to_f64 / 255.0
b1 = @b.to_f64 / 255.0

max_c = {r1, g1, b1}.max
min_c = {r1, g1, b1}.min
delta = max_c - min_c

l = (max_c + min_c) / 2.0

if delta < 0.00001
  return {0.0, 0.0, l}
end

s = l > 0.5 ? delta / ((2.0 - max_c) - min_c) : delta / (max_c + min_c)

h = if max_c == r1
  ((g1 - b1) / delta) + (g1 < b1 ? 6.0 : 0.0)
elsif max_c == g1
  ((b1 - r1) / delta) + 2.0
else
  ((r1 - g1) / delta) + 4.0
end
h = h * 60.0

{h, s, l}

grp << bg

if p >= 0.9999
  fg = Celestine::Circle.new
  fg.cx = cx
  fg.cy = cy
  fg.radius = radius
  fg.fill = "none"
  fg.stroke = fill_color
  fg.stroke_width = stroke_width
  grp << fg
elsif p > 0.001
  deg2rad = ::Math::PI / 180.0
  a1 = start_angle * deg2rad
  a2 = (start_angle + (p * 360.0)) * deg2rad

instance_methods.summary: Draws a sparkline trend graph for numeric time-series data
instance_methods.args_string: (data : Array(Number), x : Number, y : Number, width : Number, height : Number, stroke : String = "#0284c7", stroke_width : Number = 2, fill : String | Nil = nil, smooth : Bool = false, &block : Celestine::Path -> ) : Celestine::Path

def.name: sparkline
def.body:
path = Celestine::Path.new
path.stroke = stroke
path.stroke_width = stroke_width
path.fill = fill || "none"

if data.size < 2
  if data.size == 1
    path.move_to(x, y + (height / 2.0))
    path.line_to(x + width, y + (height / 2.0))
  end
  yield path
  self << path
  return path
end

min_val = data.map(&.to_f64).min
max_val = data.map(&.to_f64).max
val_range = max_val - min_val
if val_range == 0.0
  val_range = 1.0
end

n = data.size
dx = width.to_f64 / (n - 1)

pts = data.map_with_index do |val, i|
  px = x.to_f64 + (i * dx)
  normalized_y = (val.to_f64 - min_val) / val_range
  py = (y.to_f64 + height.to_f64) - (normalized_y * height.to_f64)
  {px, py}
end

path.move_to(pts[0][0], pts[0][1])

if smooth && pts.size > 2
  1.upto(pts.size - 1) do |i|
    p0 = i > 1 ? pts[i - 2] : pts[i - 1]
    p1 = pts[i - 1]
    p2 = pts[i]
    p3 = i < (pts.size - 1) ? pts[i + 1] : pts[i]

    cp1x = p1[0] + ((p2[0] - p0[0]) / 6.0)
    cp1y = p1[1] + ((p2[1] - p0[1]) / 6.0)
    cp2x = p2[0] - ((p3[0] - p1[0]) / 6.0)
    cp2y = p2[1] - ((p3[1] - p1[1]) / 6.0)

    path.curve_to(cp1x, cp1y, cp2x, cp2y, p2[0], p2[1])
  end
else
  1.upto(pts.size - 1) do |i|
    path.line_to(pts[i][0], pts[i][1])
  end
end

if fill
  path.line_to(pts.last[0], y.to_f64 + height.to_f64)
  path.line_to(pts.first[0], y.to_f64 + height.to_f64)
  path.close
end

yield path
self << path
path

class_methods.name: topic_01_drawing_basics
class_methods.doc:
**Drawing Basics & Output Targets**: How to invoke Celestine.draw to generate SVG strings or stream directly to IO.

All vector drawing starts with `Celestine.draw`. By default, it returns a finalized SVG XML `String`.
For high-performance web servers (e.g. Kemal, Lucky, Amber) or file output, pass an `IO` directly
to avoid unnecessary intermediate string allocations.

#### Working Examples

```crystal
require "celestine"

# 1. Generate an SVG String
svg_string = Celestine.draw do |ctx|
  ctx.view_box = {x: 0, y: 0, w: 100, h: 100}
  ctx.circle do |c|
    c.x = 50
    c.y = 50
    c.radius = 40
    c.fill = "#ff007f"
  end
end

# 2. Stream directly to an IO (e.g. File or HTTP response)
File.open("output.svg", "w") do |file|
  Celestine.draw(file) do |ctx|
    ctx.rectangle do |r|
      r.width = 100
      r.height = 100
      r.fill = "blue"
    end
  end
end
```

class_methods.name: topic_02_dsl_vs_object_model
class_methods.doc:
**Block DSL vs Explicit Object Model**: Comparing context builder blocks with explicit object instantiation.

Celestine supports two interchangeable workflows:

1. **Fluent Block DSL**: Inside `Celestine.draw do |ctx|`, invoke helper methods such as
   `ctx.circle`, `ctx.rectangle`, `ctx.path`, or `ctx.group`. Each method yields a fresh instance
   of the element.
2. **Explicit Object Model**: Create any drawable using standard `.new` constructors (e.g. `Celestine::Circle.new`),
   configure its properties, and append it to any container using `<<`.

#### Working Examples

```crystal
Celestine.draw do |ctx|
  # Approach A: Context helper block
  ctx.rectangle do |r|
    r.x = 10
    r.y = 10
    r.width = 80
    r.height = 40
    r.fill = "#3799FB"
  end

  # Approach B: Explicit object creation
  c = Celestine::Circle.new
  c.x = 50
  c.y = 50
  c.radius = 25
  c.fill = "#0353A4"
  ctx << c
end
```

class_methods.name: topic_03_element_reuse_and_defs
class_methods.doc:
**Reusing Elements with Definitions & Use**: Defining reusable assets in <defs> and instantiating them via <use>.

To prevent duplicating complex geometry or styles, define elements in the document's `<defs>`
collection by passing `define: true` to DSL methods, or by calling `ctx.define(element)`.
Elements can then be referenced anywhere in the document using `ctx.use`.

#### Working Examples

```crystal
Celestine.draw do |ctx|
  # Define a reusable star symbol in <defs>
  ctx.path(define: true) do |p|
    p.id = "star-shape"
    p.a_move(10, 1)
    p.a_line(4, 19)
    p.a_line(19, 7)
    p.a_line(1, 7)
    p.a_line(16, 19)
    p.close
    p.fill = "gold"
  end

  # Clone the defined star at multiple coordinates
  ctx.use("star-shape") do |u|
    u.x = 10
    u.y = 10
  end

  ctx.use("star-shape") do |u|
    u.x = 50
    u.y = 10
    u.opacity = 0.5
  end
end
```

#### Common Pitfalls & Safety Caveats

- **Warning**: Reused drawables MUST have an ID assigned before calling ctx.use.
- **Warning**: Properties set on <use> override presentation attributes of the referenced element according to SVG cascading rules.

class_methods.name: topic_01_filter_primitives
class_methods.doc:
**Filter Pipelines & fe* Primitives**: Constructing multi-stage filter pipelines using feGaussianBlur, feColorMatrix, and more. Celestine implements 16 W3C filter primitives under `Celestine::Filter`. Filters are declared using `ctx.filter` (automatically placed into ``) and assigned to shapes using `.set_filter(id)`.
Primitive Celestine Method Description
`feGaussianBlur` `f.blur` Standard Gaussian blur with stdDeviation
`feColorMatrix` `f.color_matrix` Matrix, saturate, hueRotate, luminanceToAlpha
`feDropShadow` `f.drop_shadow` Combined blur and offset drop shadow
`feDisplacementMap` `f.displacement_map` Geometric distortion using map channels
`feTurbulence` `f.turbulence` Perlin noise and fractal noise generation
`feBlend` `f.blend` Blend modes (multiply, screen, overlay, etc.)
`feComposite` `f.composite` Porter-Duff compositing operators
`feComponentTransfer` `f.component_transfer` Linear, gamma, and table color curves
`feMorphology` `f.morphology` Erode and dilate operators
`feOffset` `f.offset` Spatial translation of graphic buffers
`feTile` `f.tile` Repeats input image to fill filter region
`feFlood` `f.flood` Solid color flood fill
`feSpecularLighting` `f.specular_lighting` Surface lighting bump-mapping
#### Working Examples ```crystal svg = Celestine.draw do |ctx| ctx.filter do |f| f.id = "soft-glow" f.blur do |b| b.input = Celestine::Filter::SOURCE_GRAPHIC b.std_deviation = 5 b.result = "blur-out" end f.merge do |m| m.add_node("blur-out") m.add_node(Celestine::Filter::SOURCE_GRAPHIC) end end ctx.circle do |c| c.x = 100 c.y = 100 c.radius = 40 c.fill = "#00f0ff" c.set_filter("soft-glow") end end ```
class_methods.summary: Filter Pipelines & fe Primitives*: Constructing multi-stage filter pipelines using feGaussianBlur, feColorMatrix, and more.

class_methods.name: topic_02_gradients_and_patterns
class_methods.doc:
**Gradients & Patterns**: Configuring smooth color transitions and repeating visual fills.

Gradients define smooth color transitions across shapes. Celestine supports both linear and radial
gradients, which can be bound directly via `shape.set_fill(gradient)`.

#### Working Examples

```crystal
svg = Celestine.draw do |ctx|
  grad = ctx.linear_gradient do |g|
    g.id = "sunset"
    g.stop(0, color: "#ff512f")
    g.stop(1, color: "#dd2476")
  end

  ctx.rectangle do |r|
    r.width = 200
    r.height = 100
    r.set_fill(grad)
  end
end
```
class_methods.summary: Gradients & Patterns: Configuring smooth color transitions and repeating visual fills.

class_methods.name: topic_03_smil_animations
class_methods.doc:
**Declarative SMIL Animations**: Animating attributes, transforms, and motion paths without JavaScript.

Every drawable can host SMIL animation tags:
- `shape.animate`: Animates attributes like `opacity`, `fill`, `r`, `width`.
- `shape.animate_motion`: Moves shapes along arbitrary SVG path trajectories.
- `shape.animate_transform_*`: Hardware-accelerated rotations, scaling, and translations.

class_methods.name: topic_01_fluent_paths
class_methods.doc:
**Fluent Path Construction**: Chainable movement, lines, curves, and arcs with Point and Tuple overloads.

Rather than relying solely on cryptic SVG command codes, `Celestine::Path` supports
fluent chaining where every command returns `self`.

Supported commands include:
- `move_to(x, y)` / `move_to(point)` / `move_by(dx, dy)`
- `line_to(x, y)` / `line_to(point)` / `line_by(dx, dy)`
- `horizontal_to(x)` / `vertical_to(y)`
- `curve_to(c1x, c1y, c2x, c2y, x, y)` / `smooth_curve_to(...)`
- `quad_to(cx, cy, x, y)` / `smooth_quad_to(...)`
- `arc_to(rx, ry, rotation, large, sweep, x, y)` / `arc_by(...)`
- `close` or `close_path`

#### Working Examples

```crystal
Celestine.draw do |ctx|
  ctx.path do |p|
    p.stroke = "#0284c7"
    p.fill = "none"
    p.move_to(10, 20)
     .line_to(100, 20)
     .curve_to(120, 20, 150, 50, 150, 80)
     .close
  end
end
```
class_methods.summary: Fluent Path Construction: Chainable movement, lines, curves, and arcs with Point and Tuple overloads.

class_methods.name: topic_02_procedural_shapes
class_methods.doc:
**Procedural Shape Generators**: Instantly build stars, regular polygons, annular arc sectors, rounded rects, and hearts.

Paths can procedurally generate complex vector geometries in a single call:

- `regular_polygon(cx, cy, sides, radius)`
- `star(cx, cy, points, outer_radius, inner_radius)`
- `arc_sector(cx, cy, r_inner, r_outer, start_angle, end_angle)`
- `rounded_rect(x, y, width, height, rx, ry)`
- `heart(cx, cy, size)`

#### Working Examples

```crystal
Celestine.draw do |ctx|
  ctx.path do |p|
    p.fill = "#f59e0b"
    p.star(cx: 100, cy: 100, points: 5, outer_radius: 50, inner_radius: 25)
  end
end
```
class_methods.summary: Procedural Shape Generators: Instantly build stars, regular polygons, annular arc sectors, rounded rects, and hearts.

class_methods.name: topic_03_turtle_graphics
class_methods.doc:
**Turtle Graphics**: Relative angle and distance path generation.

Use the integrated `turtle` engine to draw algorithmic geometries using relative forward
steps and angle turns.

#### Working Examples

```crystal
Celestine.draw do |ctx|
  ctx.path do |p|
    p.stroke = "#10b981"
    p.turtle(start_x: 100, start_y: 100) do |t|
      4.times do
        t.forward(80)
         .turn_right(90)
      end
      t.close
    end
  end
end
```
class_methods.summary: Turtle Graphics: Relative angle and distance path generation.

class_methods.name: topic_01_rough_dsl
class_methods.doc:
**Using the Rough Builder DSL**: Block-based hand-drawn vector graphics.

The `ctx.rough` method configures the sketching engine and provides a convenient
builder block:

- `roughness`: controls degree of jitter and multi-pass displacement (default 1.0)
- `bowing`: controls curve bowing deflection (default 1.0)
- `seed`: provides deterministic generation across renders

#### Working Examples

```crystal
Celestine.draw do |ctx|
  ctx.rough(roughness: 1.5, stroke: "#334155", stroke_width: 2) do |r|
    r.rect(20, 20, 160, 100)
    r.circle(260, 70, 40)
    r.line(20, 160, 300, 160)
    r.polygon([{40, 200}, {100, 180}, {80, 240}])
  end
end
```
class_methods.summary: Using the Rough Builder DSL: Block-based hand-drawn vector graphics.

class_methods.name: topic_02_direct_path_sketching
class_methods.doc:
**Direct Path Sketching**: Applying sketchy primitives to any existing Path drawable.

Any `Celestine::Path` can directly invoke `rough_line`, `rough_rect`, `rough_circle`,
or `rough_polygon`.

#### Working Examples

```crystal
Celestine.draw do |ctx|
  ctx.path do |p|
    p.stroke = "#e11d48"
    p.rough_circle(cx: 100, cy: 100, r: 50, roughness: 1.2)
  end
end
```

class_methods.args_string: (start_angle, end_angle, distance, thickness = 10, large = false, flip = false)
class_methods.args_html: (start_angle, end_angle, distance, thickness = 10, large = false, flip = false)

def.name: make_arc
def.body:
p1 = Celestine::FPoint.new(0 + 250, distance + 250)
p2 = Celestine::FPoint.new(0 + 250, (distance + thickness) + 250)

p1_t1 = Celestine::Math.rotate_point(p1.x, p1.y, SCREEN_SIZE / 2.0, SCREEN_SIZE / 2.0, start_angle)
p2_t1 = Celestine::Math.rotate_point(p2.x, p2.y, SCREEN_SIZE / 2.0, SCREEN_SIZE / 2.0, end_angle)

path = Celestine::Path.new
path.a_move(p1_t1.x, p1_t1.y)

current_p1_angle = start_angle
while current_p1_angle <= end_angle
  if current_p1_angle > end_angle
    current_p1_angle = end_angle
  end
  p1_r1 = Celestine::Math.rotate_point(p1.x, p1.y, SCREEN_SIZE / 2.0, SCREEN_SIZE / 2.0, current_p1_angle)
  path.a_line(p1_r1.x.round(PRECISION), p1_r1.y.round(PRECISION))
  current_p1_angle = current_p1_angle + ARC_PRECISION
end
path.a_line(p2_t1.x.round(PRECISION), p2_t1.y.round(PRECISION))

current_p2_angle = end_angle
while current_p2_angle >= start_angle
  if current_p2_angle < start_angle
    current_p2_angle = start_angle
  end
  p2_r1 = Celestine::Math.rotate_point(p2.x, p2.y, SCREEN_SIZE / 2.0, SCREEN_SIZE / 2.0, current_p2_angle)
  path.a_line(p2_r1.x.round(PRECISION), p2_r1.y.round(PRECISION))
  current_p2_angle = current_p2_angle - ARC_PRECISION
end

path.close

path

def.name: arc_sector
def.body:
deg2rad = ::Math::PI / 180.0
a1 = start_angle * deg2rad
a2 = end_angle * deg2rad
span = (end_angle - start_angle).abs
large_arc = span > 180.0

p_in_start_x = cx + (r_inner * (::Math.cos(a1)))
p_in_start_y = cy + (r_inner * (::Math.sin(a1)))
p_in_end_x = cx + (r_inner * (::Math.cos(a2)))
p_in_end_y = cy + (r_inner * (::Math.sin(a2)))

p_out_start_x = cx + (r_outer * (::Math.cos(a1)))
p_out_start_y = cy + (r_outer * (::Math.sin(a1)))
p_out_end_x = cx + (r_outer * (::Math.cos(a2)))
p_out_end_y = cy + (r_outer * (::Math.sin(a2)))

move_to(p_out_start_x, p_out_start_y)
arc_to(r_outer, r_outer, rotation: 0, large: large_arc, sweep: true, x: p_out_end_x, y: p_out_end_y)
line_to(p_in_end_x, p_in_end_y)
arc_to(r_inner, r_inner, rotation: 0, large: large_arc, sweep: false, x: p_in_start_x, y: p_in_start_y)
close

def.name: regular_polygon

if sides < 3
  raise(ArgumentError.new("Polygon must have at least 3 sides"))
end
angle_step = (360.0 / sides) * (::Math::PI / 180.0)
base_angle = start_angle * (::Math::PI / 180.0)

sides.times do |i|
  angle = base_angle + (i * angle_step)
  px = cx + (radius * (::Math.cos(angle)))
  py = cy + (radius * (::Math.sin(angle)))
  if i == 0
    move_to(px, py)
  else
    line_to(px, py)
  end
end

def.name: circle
def.body:
if r <= 0
  return
end
rad = r.to_f64
center_x = cx.to_f64
center_y = cy.to_f64


@passes.times do
  points_count = 8
  angle_step = (::Math::PI * 2.0) / points_count
  pts = Array(Tuple(Float64, Float64)).new(points_count + 1)

  (points_count + 1).times do |i|
    angle = i * angle_step
    r_jitter = rad + (rand_offset(@max_random_offset * 1.2))
    px = center_x + (r_jitter * (::Math.cos(angle)))
    py = center_y + (r_jitter * (::Math.sin(angle)))
    pts << {px, py}
  end


  path.move_to(pts[0][0], pts[0][1])
  1.upto(points_count) do |i|
    curr = pts[i]
    prev = pts[i - 1]
    mid_x = (prev[0] + curr[0]) / 2.0
    mid_y = (prev[1] + curr[1]) / 2.0
    path.quad_to(prev[0], prev[1], mid_x, mid_y)
  end
  path.line_to(pts.last[0], pts.last[1])
end

def.body:
dx = (x2 - x1).to_f64
dy = (y2 - y1).to_f64
len = ::Math.sqrt((dx * dx) + (dy * dy))
if len < 0.001
  return
end

nx = (-dy) / len
ny = dx / len

@passes.times do

  overshoot = rand_offset(@max_random_offset * 1.5)
  sx = (x1.to_f64 + (rand_offset(@max_random_offset))) - (((dx / len) * overshoot) * 0.5)
  sy = (y1.to_f64 + (rand_offset(@max_random_offset))) - (((dy / len) * overshoot) * 0.5)
  ex = (x2.to_f64 + (rand_offset(@max_random_offset))) + (((dx / len) * overshoot) * 0.5)
  ey = (y2.to_f64 + (rand_offset(@max_random_offset))) + (((dy / len) * overshoot) * 0.5)


  bow = rand_offset((@bowing * @max_random_offset) * 1.2)
  cx = ((x1 + x2) / 2.0) + (nx * bow)
  cy = ((y1 + y2) / 2.0) + (ny * bow)

  path.move_to(sx, sy)
  path.quad_to(cx, cy, ex, ey)
end

instance_methods.name: draw
instance_methods.doc: Main draw method for a drawable. Takes in and interacts with an io.
instance_methods.summary: Main draw method for a drawable.

def.name: draw
def.body:
((io << '<') << TAG) << ' '
draw_attributes(io)

if dominant_baseline
  io << "dominant-baseline=\"#{dominant_baseline}\" "
end
if text_anchor
  io << "text-anchor=\"#{text_anchor}\" "
end
if dx
  io << "dx=\"#{dx}#{dx_units}\" "
end
if dy
  io << "dy=\"#{dy}#{dy_units}\" "
end
if rotate.empty?
else
  io << "rotate=\""
  rotate.join(io, " ")
  io << "\" "
end
if length
  io << "textLength=\"#{length}#{length_units}\" "
end
if length_adjust
  io << "lengthAdjust=\"#{length_adjust}\" "
end
if font_family
  io << "font-family=\"#{font_family}\" "
end
if font_size
  io << "font-size=\"#{font_size}#{font_size_units}\" "
end
if font_size_adjust
  io << "font-size-adjust=\"#{font_size_adjust}\" "
end
if font_stretch
  io << "font-stretch=\"#{font_stretch}\" "
end
if font_style
  io << "font-style=\"#{font_style}\" "
end
if font_variant
  io << "font-variant=\"#{font_variant}\" "
end
if font_weight
  io << "font-weight=\"#{font_weight}\" "
end
if letter_spacing
  io << "letter-spacing=\"#{letter_spacing}#{letter_spacing_units}\" "
end

if text
  inner_elements << text
end
if !has_inner_elements?
  io << "/>"
else
  io << '>'
  io << inner_elements
  ((io << "</") << TAG) << '>'
end
